name: empty-email-permitted-allows-anything-invalid
description: An empty-IA5String rfc822Name permitted subtree. RFC 5280 4.2.1.10 does not normatively specify what an empty rfc822Name constraint base means, and implementations diverge: Go's emailConstraints delegates the domain part to dnsConstraints.all and accepts every mailbox; OpenSSL's nc_email has no empty-base short-circuit (the 'Empty matches everything' line is only in nc_dns), so an empty permitted rfc822Name base matches no real mailbox and OpenSSL rejects the chain as a permitted-subtree violation. The verdict here is contested - the file is labeled invalid only to match the stricter (OpenSSL) reading; treat the inter-validator divergence as the load-bearing observation.
references: Go src/crypto/x509/constraints.go emailConstraints (delegates domain part to dnsConstraints.all)
OpenSSL crypto/x509/v3_ncons.c nc_email (no 'Empty matches everything' branch)
notes: DER: SEQUENCE { [0] SEQUENCE { SEQUENCE { [1] '' } } } encodes name constraints with one permittedSubtree containing rfc822Name(''). Injected via unknown_extensions because Python cryptography rejects RFC822Name('').
Go: dnsConstraints.all short-circuits the domain-part match; the leaf's mailbox matches the permitted subtree and the chain is accepted.
OpenSSL: nc_email compares the leaf rfc822Name against the constraint string; an empty constraint matches no mailbox, so the leaf falls outside permittedSubtrees and the chain is rejected.
GnuTLS: accepts. As with check_dns_constraints, an empty permitted entry is treated as 'not a permit' and skipped; with no other permitted rfc822Name entries the chain falls through to accept.
